40 41 42 # MiniMax H3 43 44 ## News 45 Offical skills to improve prompt writing: [skills on github](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/skills) 46 47 ## Online API 48 Use MiniMax\-H3 directly via API\. 49 - Global: [platform\.minimax\.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) \| CN: [platform\.minimaxi\.com](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) 50 51 ## Online App 52 Use MiniMax\-H3 directly via App\. 53 - WebApp Global: [hailuoai\.video](https://hailuoai.video/tools/minimax-h3) \| CN: [hailuoai\.com](https://hailuoai.com/) 54 - Desktop Global: [hub\.minimax\.io](https://hub.minimax.io/) \| CN: [hub\.minimaxi\.com](https://hub.minimaxi.com/) 55 56 ## System Overview 57 MiniMax H3 is a general-purpose, omni-modal generative system. It supports unified understanding of multimodal contexts composed of text, images, video, and audio, and can generate video with native stereo audio at resolutions up to 2K and durations of up to 15 seconds. Thanks to its task-generalization-oriented system design, H3 already possesses broad multimodal context understanding and generation capabilities at the pre-training stage, enabling outstanding performance in following complex multimodal instructions. 58 59 H3 supports the following input and output specifications: 60 61 | Category | Specification | 62 |---|---| 63 | Output duration | 4–15 seconds | 64 | Output aspect ratio | Supports a wide range of aspect ratios, including but not limited to 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, and 9:16 | 65 | Output resolution | Supports various resolution dimensions. The shorter side is set to 768 pixels by default. 2K \| generation can be achieved with H3-Regenerate-2K | 66 | Output frame rate | 24 FPS | 67 | Output audio | 32 kHz stereo | 68 | Supported dialogue languages | Stable support for 11 languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish. Additional languages are also supported to varying degrees | 69 70 ### Model Variants and Input Specifications 71 72 | Model Variant | Input Mode | Specifications | 73 |---|---|---| 74 | H3-Base-FL2VA | First-and-last-frame mode | Supports zero, one, or two input images.

- No image input: Text-to-video mode
- One image input: First-frame-to-video or last-frame-to-video generation
- Two image inputs: First-and-last-frame-to-video generation | 75 | H3-Base-Ref2VA | Omni-reference mode | Supports multi-modal reference inputs:

- **Images:** ≤ 9 images
- **Videos:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Audio:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Mixed inputs:** Maximum number of files across all input types is 12 | 76 77 ![Image](assets/overview.png) 78 79 The complete H3 system consists of the following three modules: 80 - H3-Context-IR: As inputs become increasingly complex, we build a dedicated system to deeply understand and refine the input multimodal instructions, then convert them into a form that H3 can readily understand—the Context Intermediate Representation—for generation. **H3-Context-IR is critical to the quality of the final output, so we strongly recommend incorporating it into your generation pipeline or following the “Prompting Guidance” to build your own context-processing system.** 81 - H3-Base: Generates audio and video based on the H3-Context-IR output, producing results at 768p resolution. 82 - H3-Regenerate-2K: Feeds the 768p result together with the original context back into H3 to regenerate the output at 2K resolution. This process leverages both H3’s powerful generative capabilities and the rich information contained in the original context, enabling it to produce high-resolution outputs with more accurate details and greater visual fidelity. 83 84 ## Model Architecture 85 86 ### H3\-Context\-IR 87 88 H3\-Context\-IR is a hosted preprocessing and orchestration system designed for free\-form multimodal inputs\. 89 90 It interprets the relationships among text, images, audio, and reference videos, as well as how these materials relate to the intended generation output\. Its internal workflow includes instruction parsing, cross\-modal association, temporal understanding, and complex logical reasoning\. 91 92 H3\-Context\-IR serializes its understanding of the context into a structured representation accepted by H3\-Base\. Without deviating from the user’s original intent, it may also supplement missing or underspecified semantic details where appropriate\. 93 94 Because H3\-Context\-IR relies on a multi\-stage workflow and multiple hosted models and services, it is not included in this open\-source release\. We provide an API that enables users to reproduce the behavior of the official workflow\. We also provide detailed tutorials, and developers can follow the **Prompting Guidance** to build their own preprocessing systems\. 95 96 For detailed usage instructions, see **Recommended Workflow — Full 2K Workflow**\. 97 98 **Safety Guardrails** 99 100 User\-submitted text, images and videos, as well as enhanced prompts, are subject to automated moderation\. Content suspected of being unlawful, pornographic, or infringing third\-party rights may be blocked\. We use industry\-standard filtering measures but cannot eliminate false positives or false negatives\. These guardrails do not affect the Licensee’s obligations under the MiniMax H3 Community License, especially those relating to lawful use and use restrictions\. 101 102 ### H3\-Base 103 104 ![Image](assets/full-arch.png) 105 106 #### Architecture Overview 107 108 - H3\-Base encodes different modalities using their corresponding encoders or VAEs and organizes the encoded representations into a unified packed multimodal sequence\. RoPE is used to capture the necessary spatial and temporal relationships among tokens before the entire sequence is passed to the H3\-Omni\-Transformer\. 109 110 - Specifically, text is encoded by the H3\-Encoder; visual inputs are encoded by both the H3\-Encoder and the H3\-VisualVAE; and audio is encoded solely by the H3\-AudioVAE\. 111 112 - The H3\-Omni\-Transformer jointly predicts video and audio latents, which are then decoded into video and stereo audio, respectively\. 113 114 - To reduce the computational cost of long multimodal sequences, H3 natively supports sparse\-attention training and inference\. The initial open\-source release provides inference with full attention only\. Our sparse\-attention implementation will be released in a future update\. 115 116 #### H3\-Encoder 117 118 - The H3\-Encoder uses the full pretrained weights of Qwen3\-VL\-32B and provides the hidden states from its 50th layer to the H3\-Omni\-Transformer\. 119 120 - We add several special tokens, such as ``, to the tokenizer configuration\. When using H3, the tokenizer and associated configuration files provided in the H3 repository are required\. 121 122 #### H3\-VAE 123 124 H3 uses separate visual and audio latents to represent their respective modalities\. 125 126 ##### H3\-VisualVAE 127 128 - H3\-VisualVAE is a temporally causal video autoencoder with a spatial compression factor of 16×, a temporal compression factor of 4×, and 24 latent channels, denoted as f16t4d24\. We apply several latent\-space optimization techniques to jointly improve reconstruction quality and latent learnability\. 129 130 - Before being passed to the H3\-Omni\-Transformer, the visual latents are further patchified with a patch size of `1 × 2 × 2` along the `(time, height, width)` dimensions\. As a result, the visual tokens entering the Transformer have an effective spatial downsampling factor of 32×, while the temporal downsampling factor remains 4×\. 131 132 - The latent space of H3\-VisualVAE is optimized for both reconstruction quality and ease of learning by the generative model\. After training its encoder, we additionally train a ViT\-based decoder to reduce decoding costs and further improve reconstruction quality\. 133 134 ##### H3\-AudioVAE 135 136 - H3-AudioVAE uses the same encoder and decoder for both the left and right audio channels while processing each channel independently. The decoded channels are then recombined, enabling stereo audio input and output. 137 - For each channel, H3-AudioVAE compresses 32 kHz audio into a sequence of latent tokens with a temporal rate of 40 Hz. 138 - Inspired by VA-VAE, we optimize the latent space to preserve audio reconstruction quality while making it easier for the generative model to learn. 139 140 #### H3\-Omni\-Transformer 141 142 - For scalability and generalization, we adopt a relatively simple Transformer block design\. H3\-Omni\-Transformer is a 33B\-parameter dense, single\-stream Transformer, with approximately 13B parameters residing in AdaLN\-related branches\. Because the AdaLN modulation outputs can be precomputed and cached, these parameters do not need to be loaded for inference\-only deployment\. We release the complete model weights to support further development, including fine\-tuning\. 143 144 - Neither the attention layers nor the FFN layers contain modality\-specific structures\. Modality\-specific parameters are confined to the input/output layers and the AdaLN branches\. In particular, modality\-specific AdaLN improves generation quality with relatively low additional training and inference costs\. 145 146 - The model uses three\-dimensional Multimodal Rotary Position Embeddings \(MM\-RoPE\) to represent positional relationships across the temporal and two spatial dimensions, `(t, h, w)`\. 147 148 - During the final stage of training, we introduce native sparse attention to reduce the computational cost of long sequences\. The sparse\-attention implementation is not included in the initial open\-source release and will be published separately in a future update\. 149 150 151 152 ### H3-Regenerate-2K 153 154 - For H3's 2K\-resolution output, instead of using a conventional dedicated super\-resolution module, we use the H3 base model to regenerate its own low\-resolution result through an in\-context manner\. 155 156 - This approach provides two advantages: \(1\) the regeneration process can reuse the generative capabilities of H3 base model to the greatest extent possible; and \(2\) the in\-context format can reuse the original multimodal context when producing high\-resolution output, allowing it to recover information that conventional super\-resolution methods would otherwise have to “guess,” such as small text and fine details\. 157 158 - In\-context regeneration is also an example of task generalization\. 159 160 - **Due to the complexity of the system, this module is not yet open\-sourced\. We will release it once it is ready\.** We provide an API for validating the official results; see "Full 2K Workflow" below\. 161 162 163 164 ## Recommended Workflow 165 166 To help the community deploy MiniMax H3 correctly, we provide two validation methods\. 167 168 Since the complete H3 system consists of three modules—H3\-Context\-IR, H3\-Base, and H3\-Regenerate\-2K—the “Full 2K Workflow” provides an end\-to\-end validation pipeline for 2K output, combining the Open Platform API with a locally deployed H3\-Base\. The “Local Deployment of H3\-Base” section provides a method for validating 768p output using only a locally deployed H3\-Base\. 169 170 In addition, the “Prompting Guidance” section provides a detailed tutorial to help the community develop their own prompting systems\. 171 172 ### Local Deployment of H3\-Base 173 174 MiniMax H3 is released as two task\-specific checkpoints\. Each checkpoint contains a specialized Omni Transformer Model together with the required processor, tokenizer, text encoder, Visual VAE, and standalone Audio VAE components\. 175 176 |Checkpoint|Supported Tasks|Input Conditions|Output|Precision| 177 |---|---|---|---|---| 178 |MiniMax\-H3 Base FL2VA|Text\-to\-Audio\-Video \(`t2va`\), First/Last\-Frame\-to\-Audio\-Video \(`fl2va`\)|Text; optional first frame, last frame, or both|Video and audio|BF16| 179 |MiniMax\-H3 Base Ref2VA|Reference\-to\-Audio\-Video \(`ref2va`\)|Text with reference images, videos, and/or audio|Video and audio|BF16| 180 181 The released checkpoints are CFG-distilled Omni Transformer model weights. 182 183 Each checkpoint is distributed as a self\-contained Hugging Face\-style repository with the following components: 184 185 ```text 186 / 187 ├── model_index.json 188 ├── processor/ 189 ├── tokenizer/ 190 ├── text_encoder/ 191 ├── transformer/ 192 ├── visual_vae/ 193 └── audio_vae/ 194 ``` 195 196 Download the model. The repository hosts the original checkpoint (`FL2VA/`, `Ref2VA/`) and the diffusers format side by side, so scope the download to what your framework needs: 197 198 `model_index.json` is the repository-level public entry. The task-family-specific diffusers indexes remain under `FL2VA/model_index.json` and `Ref2VA/model_index.json`. 199 200 ```bash 201 # Original checkpoint, both task families (SGLang, vLLM): 202 hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --include "model_index.json" "FL2VA/*" "Ref2VA/*" --local-dir MiniMax-H3 203 204 # Or a single task family: 205 hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --include "model_index.json" "FL2VA/*" --local-dir MiniMax-H3 206 ``` 207 208 diffusers users do not need a manual download: `ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3")` fetches exactly the components it needs. See the [diffusers documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/minimax_h3) for loading recipes. 209 210 We recommend the following inference frameworks to serve the model: 211 212 - [SGLang](https://docs.sglang.io/) \- see [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3) 213 214 - [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) \- see [vllm recipes](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) 215 216 - [diffusers](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers) \- see [diffusers docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/minimax_h3) 217 218 - [ComfyUI](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI) \- see [Comfy tutorial](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3); use [R2V template](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/video_minimax_h3_r2v.json) / [T2V template](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/video_minimax_h3_t2v.json) 219 220 #### Sglang Deployment 221 222 Here we use sglang as a deployment example\. See the [MiniMax\-H3 deployment guide](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3#3-serve-minimax-h3) for additional deployment configurations\. 223 224 FL2VA: 225 226 ```bash 227 sglang serve \ 228 --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ 229 --num-gpus 4 \ 230 --ulysses-degree 4 \ 231 --performance-mode speed \ 232 --host 0.0.0.0 \ 233 --port 30010 \ 234 --model-variant fl2va 235 ``` 236 237 Ref2VA: 238 239 ```bash 240 sglang serve \ 241 --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ 242 --num-gpus 4 \ 243 --ulysses-degree 4 \ 244 --performance-mode speed \ 245 --host 0.0.0.0 \ 246 --port 30011 \ 247 --model-variant ref2va 248 ``` 249 250 #### Reproducible 768p cases 251 252 The following three use cases T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA demonstrate how to reproduce MiniMax\-H3 video\-audio generation\. 253 254 | Use case | Request | Result | 255 |---|---|---| 256 | T2VA | [View script](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/scripts/readme/reproducible-768p-t2va-request.sh) | [t2va.mp4](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/assets/t2va.mp4) | 257 | FL2VA | [View script](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/scripts/readme/reproducible-768p-fl2va-request.sh) | [fl2va.mp4](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/assets/fl2va.mp4) | 258 | Ref2VA | [View script](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/scripts/readme/reproducible-768p-ref2va-request.sh) | [ref2va.mp4](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/assets/ref2va.mp4) | 259 260 ### Full 2K\-Workflow 261 262 This section explains how to combine a locally deployed SGLang service with the official **H3\-Context\-IR** and **H3\-Regenerate\-2K** APIs to reproduce the quality of 2K videos generated directly by the MiniMax API\. 263 Before you begin, configure the SGLang endpoint and your MiniMax API credentials: 264 265 ```bash 266 # URL of your SGLang deployment 267 SGLANG_DEPLOYMENT_URL="" 268 269 # MiniMax API endpoint (choose one) 270 # CN 271 MINIMAX_API_BASE="https://api.minimaxi.com" 272 # Global 273 # MINIMAX_API_BASE="https://api.minimax.io" 274 275 # API token obtained from the MiniMax platform 276 TOKEN="" 277 ``` 278 279 MiniMax platform: 280 281 API docs: 282 - Create H3-2K: use /video-generation-v2-create [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) 283 - H3-Context-IR：use /video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir) 284 - H3-Regenerate-2K：use /video-generation-v2-regeneration [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-regeneration), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-regeneration) 285 286 287 The examples below encode local H3\-Base output files as Base64 Data URLs\. For production use, uploading the video to a publicly accessible URL and passing that URL as `base_video` is recommended\. 288 289 For each case below, we provide reference outputs at both 2K and 768p generated directly through the Open Platform API, making it easier to validate the results\. 290 291 #### case\-T2VA 292 293 - Type: Text-to-video 294 - Duration: 10 seconds 295 - Aspect ratio: 16:9 296 297 298 299 300 301 302 323 324 325 326 327 328

# MiniMax H3 ## News Offical skills to improve prompt writing: [skills on github](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/skills) ## Online API Use MiniMax\-H3 directly via API\. - Global: [platform\.minimax\.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) \| CN: [platform\.minimaxi\.com](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) ## Online App Use MiniMax\-H3 directly via App\. - WebApp Global: [hailuoai\.video](https://hailuoai.video/tools/minimax-h3) \| CN: [hailuoai\.com](https://hailuoai.com/) - Desktop Global: [hub\.minimax\.io](https://hub.minimax.io/) \| CN: [hub\.minimaxi\.com](https://hub.minimaxi.com/) ## System Overview MiniMax H3 is a general-purpose, omni-modal generative system. It supports unified understanding of multimodal contexts composed of text, images, video, and audio, and can generate video with native stereo audio at resolutions up to 2K and durations of up to 15 seconds. Thanks to its task-generalization-oriented system design, H3 already possesses broad multimodal context understanding and generation capabilities at the pre-training stage, enabling outstanding performance in following complex multimodal instructions. H3 supports the following input and output specifications: | Category | Specification | |---|---| | Output duration | 4–15 seconds | | Output aspect ratio | Supports a wide range of aspect ratios, including but not limited to 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, and 9:16 | | Output resolution | Supports various resolution dimensions. The shorter side is set to 768 pixels by default. 2K \| generation can be achieved with H3-Regenerate-2K | | Output frame rate | 24 FPS | | Output audio | 32 kHz stereo | | Supported dialogue languages | Stable support for 11 languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish. Additional languages are also supported to varying degrees | ### Model Variants and Input Specifications | Model Variant | Input Mode | Specifications | |---|---|---| | H3-Base-FL2VA | First-and-last-frame mode | Supports zero, one, or two input images.

- No image input: Text-to-video mode
- One image input: First-frame-to-video or last-frame-to-video generation
- Two image inputs: First-and-last-frame-to-video generation | | H3-Base-Ref2VA | Omni-reference mode | Supports multi-modal reference inputs:

- **Images:** ≤ 9 images
- **Videos:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Audio:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Mixed inputs:** Maximum number of files across all input types is 12 | ![Image](assets/overview.png) The complete H3 system consists of the following three modules: - H3-Context-IR: As inputs become increasingly complex, we build a dedicated system to deeply understand and refine the input multimodal instructions, then convert them into a form that H3 can readily understand—the Context Intermediate Representation—for generation. **H3-Context-IR is critical to the quality of the final output, so we strongly recommend incorporating it into your generation pipeline or following the “Prompting Guidance” to build your own context-processing system.** - H3-Base: Generates audio and video based on the H3-Context-IR output, producing results at 768p resolution. - H3-Regenerate-2K: Feeds the 768p result together with the original context back into H3 to regenerate the output at 2K resolution. This process leverages both H3’s powerful generative capabilities and the rich information contained in the original context, enabling it to produce high-resolution outputs with more accurate details and greater visual fidelity. ## Model Architecture ### H3\-Context\-IR H3\-Context\-IR is a hosted preprocessing and orchestration system designed for free\-form multimodal inputs\. It interprets the relationships among text, images, audio, and reference videos, as well as how these materials relate to the intended generation output\. Its internal workflow includes instruction parsing, cross\-modal association, temporal understanding, and complex logical reasoning\. H3\-Context\-IR serializes its understanding of the context into a structured representation accepted by H3\-Base\. Without deviating from the user’s original intent, it may also supplement missing or underspecified semantic details where appropriate\. Because H3\-Context\-IR relies on a multi\-stage workflow and multiple hosted models and services, it is not included in this open\-source release\. We provide an API that enables users to reproduce the behavior of the official workflow\. We also provide detailed tutorials, and developers can follow the **Prompting Guidance** to build their own preprocessing systems\. For detailed usage instructions, see **Recommended Workflow — Full 2K Workflow**\. **Safety Guardrails** User\-submitted text, images and videos, as well as enhanced prompts, are subject to automated moderation\. Content suspected of being unlawful, pornographic, or infringing third\-party rights may be blocked\. We use industry\-standard filtering measures but cannot eliminate false positives or false negatives\. These guardrails do not affect the Licensee’s obligations under the MiniMax H3 Community License, especially those relating to lawful use and use restrictions\. ### H3\-Base ![Image](assets/full-arch.png) #### Architecture Overview - H3\-Base encodes different modalities using their corresponding encoders or VAEs and organizes the encoded representations into a unified packed multimodal sequence\. RoPE is used to capture the necessary spatial and temporal relationships among tokens before the entire sequence is passed to the H3\-Omni\-Transformer\. - Specifically, text is encoded by the H3\-Encoder; visual inputs are encoded by both the H3\-Encoder and the H3\-VisualVAE; and audio is encoded solely by the H3\-AudioVAE\. - The H3\-Omni\-Transformer jointly predicts video and audio latents, which are then decoded into video and stereo audio, respectively\. - To reduce the computational cost of long multimodal sequences, H3 natively supports sparse\-attention training and inference\. The initial open\-source release provides inference with full attention only\. Our sparse\-attention implementation will be released in a future update\. #### H3\-Encoder - The H3\-Encoder uses the full pretrained weights of Qwen3\-VL\-32B and provides the hidden states from its 50th layer to the H3\-Omni\-Transformer\. - We add several special tokens, such as ``, to the tokenizer configuration\. When using H3, the tokenizer and associated configuration files provided in the H3 repository are required\. #### H3\-VAE H3 uses separate visual and audio latents to represent their respective modalities\. ##### H3\-VisualVAE - H3\-VisualVAE is a temporally causal video autoencoder with a spatial compression factor of 16×, a temporal compression factor of 4×, and 24 latent channels, denoted as f16t4d24\. We apply several latent\-space optimization techniques to jointly improve reconstruction quality and latent learnability\. - Before being passed to the H3\-Omni\-Transformer, the visual latents are further patchified with a patch size of `1 × 2 × 2` along the `(time, height, width)` dimensions\. As a result, the visual tokens entering the Transformer have an effective spatial downsampling factor of 32×, while the temporal downsampling factor remains 4×\. - The latent space of H3\-VisualVAE is optimized for both reconstruction quality and ease of learning by the generative model\. After training its encoder, we additionally train a ViT\-based decoder to reduce decoding costs and further improve reconstruction quality\. ##### H3\-AudioVAE - H3-AudioVAE uses the same encoder and decoder for both the left and right audio channels while processing each channel independently. The decoded channels are then recombined, enabling stereo audio input and output. - For each channel, H3-AudioVAE compresses 32 kHz audio into a sequence of latent tokens with a temporal rate of 40 Hz. - Inspired by VA-VAE, we optimize the latent space to preserve audio reconstruction quality while making it easier for the generative model to learn. #### H3\-Omni\-Transformer - For scalability and generalization, we adopt a relatively simple Transformer block design\. H3\-Omni\-Transformer is a 33B\-parameter dense, single\-stream Transformer, with approximately 13B parameters residing in AdaLN\-related branches\. Because the AdaLN modulation outputs can be precomputed and cached, these parameters do not need to be loaded for inference\-only deployment\. We release the complete model weights to support further development, including fine\-tuning\. - Neither the attention layers nor the FFN layers contain modality\-specific structures\. Modality\-specific parameters are confined to the input/output layers and the AdaLN branches\. In particular, modality\-specific AdaLN improves generation quality with relatively low additional training and inference costs\. - The model uses three\-dimensional Multimodal Rotary Position Embeddings \(MM\-RoPE\) to represent positional relationships across the temporal and two spatial dimensions, `(t, h, w)`\. - During the final stage of training, we introduce native sparse attention to reduce the computational cost of long sequences\. The sparse\-attention implementation is not included in the initial open\-source release and will be published separately in a future update\. ### H3-Regenerate-2K - For H3's 2K\-resolution output, instead of using a conventional dedicated super\-resolution module, we use the H3 base model to regenerate its own low\-resolution result through an in\-context manner\. - This approach provides two advantages: \(1\) the regeneration process can reuse the generative capabilities of H3 base model to the greatest extent possible; and \(2\) the in\-context format can reuse the original multimodal context when producing high\-resolution output, allowing it to recover information that conventional super\-resolution methods would otherwise have to “guess,” such as small text and fine details\. - In\-context regeneration is also an example of task generalization\. - **Due to the complexity of the system, this module is not yet open\-sourced\. We will release it once it is ready\.** We provide an API for validating the official results; see "Full 2K Workflow" below\. ## Recommended Workflow To help the community deploy MiniMax H3 correctly, we provide two validation methods\. Since the complete H3 system consists of three modules—H3\-Context\-IR, H3\-Base, and H3\-Regenerate\-2K—the “Full 2K Workflow” provides an end\-to\-end validation pipeline for 2K output, combining the Open Platform API with a locally deployed H3\-Base\. The “Local Deployment of H3\-Base” section provides a method for validating 768p output using only a locally deployed H3\-Base\. In addition, the “Prompting Guidance” section provides a detailed tutorial to help the community develop their own prompting systems\. ### Local Deployment of H3\-Base MiniMax H3 is released as two task\-specific checkpoints\. Each checkpoint contains a specialized Omni Transformer Model together with the required processor, tokenizer, text encoder, Visual VAE, and standalone Audio VAE components\. |Checkpoint|Supported Tasks|Input Conditions|Output|Precision| |---|---|---|---|---| |MiniMax\-H3 Base FL2VA|Text\-to\-Audio\-Video \(`t2va`\), First/Last\-Frame\-to\-Audio\-Video \(`fl2va`\)|Text; optional first frame, last frame, or both|Video and audio|BF16| |MiniMax\-H3 Base Ref2VA|Reference\-to\-Audio\-Video \(`ref2va`\)|Text with reference images, videos, and/or audio|Video and audio|BF16| The released checkpoints are CFG-distilled Omni Transformer model weights. Each checkpoint is distributed as a self\-contained Hugging Face\-style repository with the following components: ```text / ├── model_index.json ├── processor/ ├── tokenizer/ ├── text_encoder/ ├── transformer/ ├── visual_vae/ └── audio_vae/ ``` Download the model. The repository hosts the original checkpoint (`FL2VA/`, `Ref2VA/`) and the diffusers format side by side, so scope the download to what your framework needs: `model_index.json` is the repository-level public entry. The task-family-specific diffusers indexes remain under `FL2VA/model_index.json` and `Ref2VA/model_index.json`. ```bash # Original checkpoint, both task families (SGLang, vLLM): hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --include "model_index.json" "FL2VA/*" "Ref2VA/*" --local-dir MiniMax-H3 # Or a single task family: hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --include "model_index.json" "FL2VA/*" --local-dir MiniMax-H3 ``` diffusers users do not need a manual download: `ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3")` fetches exactly the components it needs. See the [diffusers documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/minimax_h3) for loading recipes. We recommend the following inference frameworks to serve the model: - [SGLang](https://docs.sglang.io/) \- see [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3) - [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) \- see [vllm recipes](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) - [diffusers](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers) \- see [diffusers docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/minimax_h3) - [ComfyUI](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI) \- see [Comfy tutorial](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3); use [R2V template](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/video_minimax_h3_r2v.json) / [T2V template](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/video_minimax_h3_t2v.json) #### Sglang Deployment Here we use sglang as a deployment example\. See the [MiniMax\-H3 deployment guide](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3#3-serve-minimax-h3) for additional deployment configurations\. FL2VA: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --num-gpus 4 \ --ulysses-degree 4 \ --performance-mode speed \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30010 \ --model-variant fl2va ``` Ref2VA: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --num-gpus 4 \ --ulysses-degree 4 \ --performance-mode speed \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30011 \ --model-variant ref2va ``` #### Reproducible 768p cases The following three use cases T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA demonstrate how to reproduce MiniMax\-H3 video\-audio generation\. | Use case | Request | Result | |---|---|---| | T2VA | [View script](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/scripts/readme/reproducible-768p-t2va-request.sh) | [t2va.mp4](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/assets/t2va.mp4) | | FL2VA | [View script](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/scripts/readme/reproducible-768p-fl2va-request.sh) | [fl2va.mp4](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/assets/fl2va.mp4) | | Ref2VA | [View script](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/scripts/readme/reproducible-768p-ref2va-request.sh) | [ref2va.mp4](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/assets/ref2va.mp4) | ### Full 2K\-Workflow This section explains how to combine a locally deployed SGLang service with the official **H3\-Context\-IR** and **H3\-Regenerate\-2K** APIs to reproduce the quality of 2K videos generated directly by the MiniMax API\. Before you begin, configure the SGLang endpoint and your MiniMax API credentials: ```bash # URL of your SGLang deployment SGLANG_DEPLOYMENT_URL="" # MiniMax API endpoint (choose one) # CN MINIMAX_API_BASE="https://api.minimaxi.com" # Global # MINIMAX_API_BASE="https://api.minimax.io" # API token obtained from the MiniMax platform TOKEN="" ``` MiniMax platform: API docs: - Create H3-2K: use /video-generation-v2-create [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) - H3-Context-IR：use /video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir) - H3-Regenerate-2K：use /video-generation-v2-regeneration [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-regeneration), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-regeneration) The examples below encode local H3\-Base output files as Base64 Data URLs\. 59	def _apply_rotary_emb(hidden_states: torch.Tensor, cos: torch.Tensor, sin: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
60	    r"""
61	    Rotate the leading `rotary_dim` channels of every head and pass the remaining channels through unchanged.
62	    `hidden_states` is `(batch_size, seq_len, num_heads, head_dim)` and `cos`/`sin` are `(seq_len, rotary_dim)`.
63	    """
64	    rotary_dim = cos.shape[-1]
65	    hidden_states_rotary = hidden_states[..., :rotary_dim]
66	    hidden_states_pass = hidden_states[..., rotary_dim:]
67	
68	    cos = cos.to(hidden_states.dtype)[None, :, None, :]
69	    sin = sin.to(hidden_states.dtype)[None, :, None, :]
70	    x1, x2 = hidden_states_rotary.chunk(2, dim=-1)
71	    hidden_states_rotated = torch.cat((-x2, x1), dim=-1)
72	    hidden_states_rotary = hidden_states_rotary * cos + hidden_states_rotated * sin
73	    return torch.cat((hidden_states_rotary, hidden_states_pass), dim=-1).contiguous()
74

76	class MiniMaxH3RotaryPosEmbed(nn.Module):
77	    r"""
78	    3-axis rotary embedding over the `(t, h, w)` coordinates of the packed sequence.
79	
80	    A single `inv_freq` buffer of `rope_freq_dim` frequencies is shared by the three axes. Each axis contributes
81	    `rope_freq_dim` angles, the three blocks are concatenated to `3 * rope_freq_dim` and then concatenated with
82	    themselves so that the `rotate_half` convention rotates `2 * 3 * rope_freq_dim` of the `head_dim` channels.
83	    """
84	
85	    def __init__(self, rope_freq_dim: int = 16, rope_theta: float = 10000.0):
86	        super().__init__()
87	        self.rope_freq_dim = rope_freq_dim
88	        inv_freq = 1.0 / (
89	            rope_theta ** (torch.arange(0, 2 * rope_freq_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / (2 * rope_freq_dim))
90	        )
91	        self.register_buffer("inv_freq", inv_freq, persistent=False)
92	
93	    def forward(self, position_ids: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
94	        # position_ids: (seq_len, 3) -> cos/sin: (seq_len, 2 * 3 * rope_freq_dim)
95	        position_ids = position_ids.to(torch.float32)
96	        freqs = position_ids.unsqueeze(-1) * self.inv_freq.view(1, 1, -1)  # (seq_len, 3, rope_freq_dim)
97	        freqs_t, freqs_h, freqs_w = freqs.unbind(dim=1)
98	        freqs = torch.cat((freqs_t, freqs_h, freqs_w), dim=-1)
99	        freqs = torch.cat((freqs, freqs), dim=-1)
100	        return freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()
101

103	class MiniMaxH3AdaLayerNormModulation(nn.Module):
104	    r"""
105	    Projects the shared timestep embedding into the six per-(timestep, modality) modulation parameters of one
106	    transformer block.
107	
108	    `(num_timesteps, time_embed_dim)` -> six tensors of shape `(num_timesteps * MINIMAX_H3_MODALITY_NUM, hidden_size)`,
109	    in the diffusers `shift_msa, scale_msa, gate_msa, shift_mlp, scale_mlp, gate_mlp` order. The row layout of the
110	    returned tensors is `[t0_mod0, t0_mod1, t0_mod2, t1_mod0, ...]`, which is what `timestep_indices *
111	    MINIMAX_H3_MODALITY_NUM + token_tags` addresses.
112	
113	    A single projection is shared by `norm1` and `norm2` and by the three modalities, so it cannot be folded into
114	    either norm the way [`~models.normalization.AdaLayerNormZero`] does. It is therefore a block-level module of its
115	    own, named after the checkpoint's `adaln_proj`, with the modulation projection under the `linear` name diffusers
116	    uses inside every AdaLN module.
117	    """
118	
119	    def __init__(self, time_embed_dim: int, hidden_size: int):
120	        super().__init__()
121	        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
122	        self.linear = nn.Linear(time_embed_dim, 6 * hidden_size * MINIMAX_H3_MODALITY_NUM, bias=True)
123	
124	    def forward(self, temb: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
125	        # The activation runs at `temb`'s own precision — float32, since `time_embedder` is a float32 module in this
126	        # mixed-precision checkpoint — and only its result is cast down to the bfloat16 projection. Every block reads
127	        # the same `temb`, so a rounding applied before the activation biases every block's modulation parameters
128	        # identically at every sampling step, which accumulates coherently over the denoising trajectory.
129	        temb = self.linear(nn.functional.silu(temb).to(get_parameter_dtype(self.linear)))
130	        temb = temb.view(-1, 6 * self.hidden_size)
131	        return temb.chunk(6, dim=-1)
132	
133	
134	class MiniMaxH3AdaLayerNormOut(nn.Module):
135	    r"""
136	    Final norm of the packed sequence, shift/scale modulated per row.
137	
138	    Same module layout and checkpoint keys as [`~models.normalization.AdaLayerNormContinuous`] (`norm` plus a `linear`
139	    projecting the conditioning embedding to `2 * hidden_size`), with two MiniMax-H3 specifics: the modulation table
140	    holds one row per *timestep* and is addressed per row of the packed sequence rather than per batch item, and the
141	    two halves of the projection are `shift` then `scale`, the order `LTX2Transformer3DModel` and
142	    `WanTransformer3DModel` also use in their output layers.
143	    """
144	
145	    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, time_embed_dim: int, eps: float):
146	        super().__init__()
147	        self.norm = nn.RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=eps)
148	        self.linear = nn.Linear(time_embed_dim, 2 * hidden_size, bias=True)
149	
150	    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, temb: torch.Tensor, timestep_indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
151	        # As in `MiniMaxH3AdaLayerNormModulation`: activate at `temb`'s precision, cast to the projection's dtype after.
152	        shift, scale = self.linear(nn.functional.silu(temb).to(get_parameter_dtype(self.linear))).chunk(2, dim=-1)
153	        # The modulation itself stays at the block stack's precision; `forward` casts to the output heads' dtype.
154	        hidden_states = self.norm(hidden_states)
155	        return hidden_states * (1.0 + scale.index_select(0, timestep_indices)) + shift.index_select(
156	            0, timestep_indices
157	        )

160	class MiniMaxH3AttnProcessor:
161	    r"""
162	    Full self-attention over one packed sequence. There is no cross-attention anywhere in MiniMax-H3.
163	    """
164	
165	    _attention_backend = None
166	    _parallel_config = None
167	
168	    def __call__(
169	        self,
170	        attn: "MiniMaxH3Attention",
171	        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
172	        rotary_emb: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
173	        attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
174	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
175	        if attn.fused_projections:
176	            query, key, value = attn.to_qkv(hidden_states).chunk(3, dim=-1)
177	        else:
178	            query = attn.to_q(hidden_states)
179	            key = attn.to_k(hidden_states)
180	            value = attn.to_v(hidden_states)
181	
182	        query = query.unflatten(-1, (attn.heads, -1))
183	        key = key.unflatten(-1, (attn.heads, -1))
184	        value = value.unflatten(-1, (attn.heads, -1))
185	
186	        query = attn.norm_q(query)
187	        key = attn.norm_k(key)
188	
189	        if rotary_emb is not None:
190	            query = _apply_rotary_emb(query, *rotary_emb)
191	            key = _apply_rotary_emb(key, *rotary_emb)
192	
193	        # MiniMax-H3 packs one request into a single attention document, so the model passes no mask and every
194	        # attention backend stays available; `attention_mask` is here because it is the processor signature every
195	        # other one in diffusers has, and a custom processor may need it.
196	        hidden_states = dispatch_attention_fn(
197	            query,
198	            key,
199	            value,
200	            attn_mask=attention_mask,
201	            dropout_p=0.0,
202	            is_causal=False,
203	            backend=self._attention_backend,
204	            parallel_config=self._parallel_config,
205	        )
206	        hidden_states = hidden_states.flatten(2, 3).type_as(query)
207	        hidden_states = attn.to_out[0](hidden_states)
208	        hidden_states = attn.to_out[1](hidden_states)
209	        return hidden_states
210

212	class MiniMaxH3Attention(nn.Module, AttentionModuleMixin):
213	    _default_processor_cls = MiniMaxH3AttnProcessor
214	    _available_processors = [MiniMaxH3AttnProcessor]
215	
216	    def __init__(
217	        self,
218	        hidden_size: int,
219	        heads: int,
220	        dim_head: int,
221	        qk_norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
222	        processor=None,
223	    ):
224	        super().__init__()
225	        self.heads = heads
226	        self.head_dim = dim_head
227	        self.inner_dim = heads * dim_head
228	        self.use_bias = False
229	
230	        self.to_q = nn.Linear(hidden_size, self.inner_dim, bias=False)
231	        self.to_k = nn.Linear(hidden_size, self.inner_dim, bias=False)
232	        self.to_v = nn.Linear(hidden_size, self.inner_dim, bias=False)
233	        self.norm_q = nn.RMSNorm(dim_head, eps=qk_norm_eps)
234	        self.norm_k = nn.RMSNorm(dim_head, eps=qk_norm_eps)
235	        self.to_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(self.inner_dim, hidden_size, bias=False), nn.Dropout(0.0)])
236	
237	        if processor is None:
238	            processor = self._default_processor_cls()
239	        self.set_processor(processor)
240	
241	    def forward(
242	        self,
243	        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
244	        rotary_emb: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
245	        attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
246	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
247	        return self.processor(self, hidden_states, rotary_emb, attention_mask)

250	class MiniMaxH3TokenRefinerBlock(nn.Module):
251	    r"""
252	    Plain pre-norm transformer block used to refine the projected text stream. No AdaLN and no rotary embedding.
253	    """
254	
255	    def __init__(
256	        self,
257	        hidden_size: int,
258	        num_attention_heads: int,
259	        attention_head_dim: int,
260	        ffn_dim: int,
261	        norm_eps: float,
262	        qk_norm_eps: float,
263	    ):
264	        super().__init__()
265	        self.norm1 = nn.RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=norm_eps)
266	        self.attn = MiniMaxH3Attention(
267	            hidden_size=hidden_size,
268	            heads=num_attention_heads,
269	            dim_head=attention_head_dim,
270	            qk_norm_eps=qk_norm_eps,
271	        )
272	        self.norm2 = nn.RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=norm_eps)
273	        self.ff = FeedForward(hidden_size, inner_dim=ffn_dim, activation_fn="swiglu", bias=False)
274	
275	    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
276	        hidden_states = hidden_states + self.attn(self.norm1(hidden_states))
277	        hidden_states = hidden_states + self.ff(self.norm2(hidden_states))
278	        return hidden_states
279	
280	
281	class MiniMaxH3TokenRefiner(nn.Module):
282	    def __init__(
283	        self,
284	        hidden_size: int,
285	        num_attention_heads: int,
286	        attention_head_dim: int,
287	        ffn_dim: int,
288	        num_layers: int,
289	        norm_eps: float,
290	        qk_norm_eps: float,
291	        final_norm_eps: float,
292	    ):
293	        super().__init__()
294	        self.refiner_blocks = nn.ModuleList(
295	            [
296	                MiniMaxH3TokenRefinerBlock(
297	                    hidden_size=hidden_size,
298	                    num_attention_heads=num_attention_heads,
299	                    attention_head_dim=attention_head_dim,
300	                    ffn_dim=ffn_dim,
301	                    norm_eps=norm_eps,
302	                    qk_norm_eps=qk_norm_eps,
303	                )
304	                for _ in range(num_layers)
305	            ]
306	        )
307	        self.final_norm = nn.RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=final_norm_eps)
308	        self.gradient_checkpointing = False
309	
310	    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
311	        for block in self.refiner_blocks:
312	            if torch.is_grad_enabled() and self.gradient_checkpointing:
313	                hidden_states = self._gradient_checkpointing_func(block, hidden_states)
314	            else:
315	                hidden_states = block(hidden_states)
316	        return self.final_norm(hidden_states)

319	class MiniMaxH3TransformerBlock(nn.Module):
320	    r"""
321	    MiniMax-H3 block: pre-norm self-attention and feed-forward, each modulated by AdaLN parameters selected per row of
322	    the packed sequence from the `(timestep, modality)` table.
323	    """
324	
325	    def __init__(
326	        self,
327	        hidden_size: int,
328	        num_attention_heads: int,
329	        attention_head_dim: int,
330	        ffn_dim: int,
331	        time_embed_dim: int,
332	        norm_eps: float,
333	        qk_norm_eps: float,
334	    ):
335	        super().__init__()
336	        self.norm1 = nn.RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=norm_eps)
337	        self.attn = MiniMaxH3Attention(
338	            hidden_size=hidden_size,
339	            heads=num_attention_heads,
340	            dim_head=attention_head_dim,
341	            qk_norm_eps=qk_norm_eps,
342	        )
343	        self.norm2 = nn.RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=norm_eps)
344	        self.ff = FeedForward(hidden_size, inner_dim=ffn_dim, activation_fn="swiglu", bias=False)
345	        self.adaln_proj = MiniMaxH3AdaLayerNormModulation(time_embed_dim=time_embed_dim, hidden_size=hidden_size)
346	
347	    def forward(
348	        self,
349	        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
350	        temb: torch.Tensor,
351	        adaln_indices: torch.Tensor,
352	        rotary_emb: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
353	        attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
354	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
355	        shift_msa, scale_msa, gate_msa, shift_mlp, scale_mlp, gate_mlp = self.adaln_proj(temb)
356	
357	        residual = hidden_states
358	        norm_hidden_states = self.norm1(hidden_states)
359	        norm_hidden_states = norm_hidden_states * (
360	            1.0 + scale_msa.index_select(0, adaln_indices)
361	        ) + shift_msa.index_select(0, adaln_indices)
362	        attn_output = self.attn(norm_hidden_states, rotary_emb, attention_mask)
363	        hidden_states = residual + gate_msa.index_select(0, adaln_indices) * attn_output
364	
365	        residual = hidden_states
366	        norm_hidden_states = self.norm2(hidden_states)
367	        norm_hidden_states = norm_hidden_states * (
368	            1.0 + scale_mlp.index_select(0, adaln_indices)
369	        ) + shift_mlp.index_select(0, adaln_indices)
370	        ff_output = self.ff(norm_hidden_states)
371	        hidden_states = residual + gate_mlp.index_select(0, adaln_indices) * ff_output
372	
373	        return hidden_states

376	class MiniMaxH3Transformer3DModel(ModelMixin, ConfigMixin, AttentionMixin, PeftAdapterMixin, CacheMixin):
377	    r"""
378	    A Transformer model for joint video + audio generation, introduced in MiniMax-H3.
379	
380	    MiniMax-H3 runs a single stack of blocks over **one packed 1-D sequence** that holds the text condition, the
381	    conditioning image / video rows, the audio rows and the target video rows. Attention is full self-attention over
382	    that sequence; there is no cross-attention and no per-modality block weights. Modality-specific behaviour comes
383	    only from the two input patch projections, the per-row AdaLN modality tag, and the two output heads.
384	
385	    The caller is responsible for building the packed layout: patchifying the video latents, ordering the rows, and
386	    producing the `(t, h, w)` position grid, the per-row modality tags and the per-row timestep indices. The sequence
387	    carries no padding — the reference implementation pads it to a multiple of 64 for FlashAttention and splits the
388	    tail off with `cu_seqlens = [0, used, S]`, which this port has no use for — so attention runs unmasked over one
389	    document and every attention backend stays available.
390	
391	    The batch axis is a pure replication axis: the structural arguments (`timestep`, `timestep_indices`, `token_tags`,
392	    `position_ids` and the three index tensors) describe one packed layout that every batch item shares, and each item
393	    is a single attention document.
394	
395	    Args:
396	        num_attention_heads (`int`, defaults to `56`):
397	            The number of heads to use for multi-head attention.
398	        attention_head_dim (`int`, defaults to `128`):
399	            The number of channels in each attention head. Note that `num_attention_heads * attention_head_dim` is
400	            *larger* than `hidden_size` in MiniMax-H3.
401	        hidden_size (`int`, defaults to `5376`):
402	            The number of channels of the packed sequence (the residual stream).
403	        num_layers (`int`, defaults to `50`):
404	            The number of transformer blocks.
405	        num_refiner_layers (`int`, defaults to `2`):
406	            The number of token refiner blocks applied to the projected text stream.
407	        ffn_dim (`int`, defaults to `14336`):
408	            The inner dimension of the SwiGLU feed-forward layers.
409	        in_channels (`int`, defaults to `24`):
410	            The number of channels of the video latents.
411	        audio_in_channels (`int`, defaults to `32`):
412	            The number of channels of the audio latents.
413	        patch_size (`tuple[int, int, int]`, defaults to `(1, 2, 2)`):
414	            The `(t, h, w)` patch used to pack the video latents into rows.
415	        text_dim (`int`, defaults to `5120`):
416	            The number of channels of the text conditioning produced by the text encoder.
417	        freq_dim (`int`, defaults to `256`):
418	            The dimension of the sinusoidal timestep embedding. Timesteps are consumed unscaled in `[0, 1]`.
419	        time_embed_hidden_dim (`int`, defaults to `5376`):
420	            The inner dimension of the timestep MLP.
421	        time_embed_dim (`int`, defaults to `2688`):
422	            The output dimension of the timestep MLP, i.e. the input of every AdaLN projection.
423	        rope_freq_dim (`int`, defaults to `16`):
424	            The number of rotary frequencies per axis. The `(t, h, w)` axes share one `inv_freq` buffer of this length
425	            and `2 * 3 * rope_freq_dim` of the `attention_head_dim` channels are rotated.
426	        rope_theta (`float`, defaults to `10000.0`):
427	            The base of the rotary frequency schedule the `rope.inv_freq` buffer is computed from.
428	        norm_eps (`float`, defaults to `1e-5`):
429	            Epsilon of the pre-attention and pre-feed-forward norms.
430	        qk_norm_eps (`float`, defaults to `1e-5`):
431	            Epsilon of the per-head query/key norms.
432	        final_norm_eps (`float`, defaults to `1e-5`):
433	            Epsilon of the token refiner output norm and of `norm_out`.
434	    """
435	
436	    _supports_gradient_checkpointing = True
437	    _no_split_modules = ["MiniMaxH3TransformerBlock", "MiniMaxH3TokenRefinerBlock", "MiniMaxH3AdaLayerNormOut"]
438	    _repeated_blocks = ["MiniMaxH3TransformerBlock", "MiniMaxH3TokenRefinerBlock"]
439	    _skip_layerwise_casting_patterns = ["norm"]
440	    # MiniMax-H3 ships a mixed-precision checkpoint: the two input patch projections, the timestep MLP and the two
441	    # output heads are float32 while everything else (including the AdaLN projections) is bfloat16. The `rope.inv_freq`
442	    # buffer is computed rather than loaded and is kept float32 for the same reason the reference ships it float32.
443	    # Entries are matched as substrings of the parameter name, so `proj_in` / `proj_out` also cover the audio heads.
444	    _keep_in_fp32_modules = [
445	        "proj_in",
446	        "audio_proj_in",
447	        "time_embedder",
448	        "proj_out",
449	        "audio_proj_out",
450	        "rope",
451	    ]
452	    # Context parallelism shards the packed sequence, so the split cannot happen on the inputs of `forward`: the rows
453	    # of the three modalities are scattered into the packed buffer with sequence-wide indices, which only address the
454	    # full sequence. The split therefore happens once the buffer is built, at the first block, and everything that is
455	    # indexed per row of the packed sequence is split alongside it: `adaln_indices` for the block stack,
456	    # `timestep_indices` for `norm_out`, and the two `rope` outputs, which carry one row of angles each. The two output
457	    # heads gather the sequence back, because `forward` then selects the video and audio rows with sequence-wide
458	    # indices as well.
459	    #
460	    # The packed sequence carries no padding, so its length is whatever the caller packed. Splitting it across the
461	    # context parallel region requires that length to be divisible by the region size — use `ulysses_anything` or
462	    # `ring_anything` for a layout that is not.
463	    _cp_plan = {
464	        "rope": {
465	            0: ContextParallelInput(split_dim=0, expected_dims=2, split_output=True),
466	            1: ContextParallelInput(split_dim=0, expected_dims=2, split_output=True),
467	        },
468	        "transformer_blocks.0": {
469	            "hidden_states": ContextParallelInput(split_dim=1, expected_dims=3, split_output=False),
470	        },
471	        # `hidden_states` is split once and then flows from block to block already sharded, but every block reads
472	        # `adaln_indices` from `forward`'s unsharded tensor, so each of them splits its own copy.
473	        "transformer_blocks.*": {
474	            "adaln_indices": ContextParallelInput(split_dim=0, expected_dims=1, split_output=False),
475	        },
476	        "norm_out": {
477	            "timestep_indices": ContextParallelInput(split_dim=0, expected_dims=1, split_output=False),
478	        },
479	        "proj_out": ContextParallelOutput(gather_dim=1, expected_dims=3),
480	        "audio_proj_out": ContextParallelOutput(gather_dim=1, expected_dims=3),
481	    }
482	
483	    @register_to_config
484	    def __init__(
485	        self,
486	        num_attention_heads: int = 56,
487	        attention_head_dim: int = 128,
488	        hidden_size: int = 5376,
489	        num_layers: int = 50,
490	        num_refiner_layers: int = 2,
491	        ffn_dim: int = 14336,
492	        in_channels: int = 24,
493	        audio_in_channels: int = 32,
494	        patch_size: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 2, 2),
495	        text_dim: int = 5120,
496	        freq_dim: int = 256,
497	        time_embed_hidden_dim: int = 5376,
498	        time_embed_dim: int = 2688,
499	        rope_freq_dim: int = 16,
500	        rope_theta: float = 10000.0,
501	        norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
502	        qk_norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
503	        final_norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
504	    ) -> None:
505	        super().__init__()
506	
507	        video_patch_dim = in_channels * patch_size[0] * patch_size[1] * patch_size[2]
508	
509	        # 1. Per-modality input projections
510	        self.proj_in = nn.Linear(video_patch_dim, hidden_size, bias=True)
511	        self.audio_proj_in = nn.Linear(audio_in_channels, hidden_size, bias=True)
512	        self.context_embedder = nn.Linear(text_dim, hidden_size, bias=True)
513	
514	        # 2. Timestep embedding, shared by every AdaLN projection
515	        self.time_proj = Timesteps(num_channels=freq_dim, flip_sin_to_cos=True, downscale_freq_shift=0)
516	        self.time_embedder = TimestepEmbedding(
517	            in_channels=freq_dim, time_embed_dim=time_embed_hidden_dim, out_dim=time_embed_dim
518	        )
519	
520	        # 3. Rotary embedding over the packed (t, h, w) grid
521	        self.rope = MiniMaxH3RotaryPosEmbed(rope_freq_dim=rope_freq_dim, rope_theta=rope_theta)
522	
523	        # 4. Text stream refiner
524	        self.token_refiner = MiniMaxH3TokenRefiner(
525	            hidden_size=hidden_size,
526	            num_attention_heads=num_attention_heads,
527	            attention_head_dim=attention_head_dim,
528	            ffn_dim=ffn_dim,
529	            num_layers=num_refiner_layers,
530	            norm_eps=norm_eps,
531	            qk_norm_eps=qk_norm_eps,
532	            final_norm_eps=final_norm_eps,
533	        )
534	
535	        # 5. The block stack
536	        self.transformer_blocks = nn.ModuleList(
537	            [
538	                MiniMaxH3TransformerBlock(
539	                    hidden_size=hidden_size,
540	                    num_attention_heads=num_attention_heads,
541	                    attention_head_dim=attention_head_dim,
542	                    ffn_dim=ffn_dim,
543	                    time_embed_dim=time_embed_dim,
544	                    norm_eps=norm_eps,
545	                    qk_norm_eps=qk_norm_eps,
546	                )
547	                for _ in range(num_layers)
548	            ]
549	        )
550	
551	        # 6. Shared output norm and the two per-modality output heads. Both heads run over every row of the packed
552	        # sequence; the rows of each modality are selected afterwards.
553	        self.norm_out = MiniMaxH3AdaLayerNormOut(
554	            hidden_size=hidden_size, time_embed_dim=time_embed_dim, eps=final_norm_eps
555	        )
556	        self.proj_out = nn.Linear(hidden_size, video_patch_dim, bias=True)
557	        self.audio_proj_out = nn.Linear(hidden_size, audio_in_channels, bias=True)
558	
559	        self.gradient_checkpointing = False
560	
561	    @apply_lora_scale("attention_kwargs")
562	    def forward(
563	        self,
564	        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
565	        audio_hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
566	        encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
567	        timestep: torch.Tensor,
568	        timestep_indices: torch.Tensor,
569	        token_tags: torch.Tensor,
570	        position_ids: torch.Tensor,
571	        video_indices: torch.Tensor,
572	        audio_indices: torch.Tensor,
573	        text_indices: torch.Tensor,
574	        attention_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
575	        return_dict: bool = True,
576	    ) -> MiniMaxH3TransformerOutput | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
577	        r"""
578	        Args:
579	            hidden_states (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_video_tokens, in_channels * prod(patch_size))`):
580	                Patchified video latent rows — conditioning rows and target rows — ordered as they appear in the packed
581	                sequence, i.e. matching `video_indices`.
582	            audio_hidden_states (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_audio_tokens, audio_in_channels)`):
583	                Audio latent rows, ordered to match `audio_indices`.
584	            encoder_hidden_states (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_text_tokens, text_dim)`):
585	                Text conditioning, ordered to match `text_indices`.
586	            timestep (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(num_timesteps,)`):
587	                The *distinct* timestep values present in the packed sequence, in `[0, 1]` and unscaled. One forward
588	                serves rows at different noise levels (target video, target audio, conditioning rows).
589	            timestep_indices (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(seq_len,)`):
590	                For every row of the packed sequence, the index of its timestep in `timestep`.
591	            token_tags (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(seq_len,)`):
592	                For every row of the packed sequence, its modality: `0` video, `1` text, `2` audio.
593	            position_ids (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(seq_len, 3)`):
594	                The `(t, h, w)` rotary coordinates of every row of the packed sequence.
595	            video_indices (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(num_video_tokens,)`):
596	                Positions of the video rows in the packed sequence.
597	            audio_indices (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(num_audio_tokens,)`):
598	                Positions of the audio rows in the packed sequence.
599	            text_indices (`torch.Tensor` of shape `(num_text_tokens,)`):
600	                Positions of the text rows in the packed sequence.
601	            attention_kwargs (`dict`, *optional*):
602	                A kwargs dictionary that, if specified, may carry a `scale` entry which is applied to the LoRA layers.
603	            return_dict (`bool`, defaults to `True`):
604	                Whether to return a [`MiniMaxH3TransformerOutput`] instead of a plain tuple.
605	
606	        Returns:
607	            [`MiniMaxH3TransformerOutput`] or `tuple`:
608	                The video velocity of shape `(batch_size, num_video_tokens, in_channels * prod(patch_size))` and the
609	                audio velocity of shape `(batch_size, num_audio_tokens, audio_in_channels)`, in the row order of
610	                `video_indices` and `audio_indices`.
611	        """
612	        # `attention_kwargs` is consumed by the `@apply_lora_scale` decorator on this method.
613	        if position_ids.ndim != 2 or position_ids.shape[-1] != 3:
614	            raise ValueError(f"`position_ids` must be a `(seq_len, 3)` tensor, got {list(position_ids.shape)}.")
615	        sequence_length = position_ids.shape[0]
616	        if token_tags.shape != (sequence_length,) or timestep_indices.shape != (sequence_length,):
617	            raise ValueError(
618	                "`token_tags` and `timestep_indices` must both be `(seq_len,)` tensors matching `position_ids`, got "
619	                f"{list(token_tags.shape)} and {list(timestep_indices.shape)} for seq_len={sequence_length}."
620	            )
621	
622	        rotary_emb = self.rope(position_ids)
623	
624	        # 1. Project each modality and scatter the rows into the packed sequence buffer. The checkpoint is
625	        # mixed-precision (the two patch projections are float32 while `context_embedder` and the block stack are
626	        # bfloat16 — see `_keep_in_fp32_modules`), so every input is aligned with its projection's parameter dtype,
627	        # mirroring the reference's explicit casts. The text stream sets the dtype of the packed sequence.
628	        video_embeds = self.proj_in(hidden_states.to(get_parameter_dtype(self.proj_in)))
629	        audio_embeds = self.audio_proj_in(audio_hidden_states.to(get_parameter_dtype(self.audio_proj_in)))
630	        text_embeds = self.context_embedder(encoder_hidden_states.to(get_parameter_dtype(self.context_embedder)))
631	        text_embeds = self.token_refiner(text_embeds)
632	
633	        hidden_states = text_embeds.new_zeros((text_embeds.shape[0], sequence_length, text_embeds.shape[-1]))
634	        hidden_states = hidden_states.index_copy(1, text_indices, text_embeds)
635	        hidden_states = hidden_states.index_copy(1, video_indices, video_embeds.to(text_embeds.dtype))
636	        hidden_states = hidden_states.index_copy(1, audio_indices, audio_embeds.to(text_embeds.dtype))
637	
638	        # 2. One timestep embedding per distinct noise level. `temb` is shared by all AdaLN projections, which are
639	        # bfloat16 in the checkpoint while `time_embedder` is float32, so it stays at the time embedder's precision:
640	        # each AdaLN module applies its own activation to it and casts to its projection's dtype afterwards.
641	        temb = self.time_proj(timestep)
642	        temb = self.time_embedder(temb.to(get_parameter_dtype(self.time_embedder)))
643	
644	        # 3. Row -> AdaLN table row.
645	        adaln_indices = timestep_indices * MINIMAX_H3_MODALITY_NUM + token_tags
646	
647	        for block in self.transformer_blocks:
648	            if torch.is_grad_enabled() and self.gradient_checkpointing:
649	                hidden_states = self._gradient_checkpointing_func(
650	                    block, hidden_states, temb, adaln_indices, rotary_emb
651	                )
652	            else:
653	                hidden_states = block(hidden_states, temb, adaln_indices, rotary_emb)
654	
655	        # 5. Both heads run over every row, then the rows of each modality are selected. The heads are listed in
656	        # `_keep_in_fp32_modules`, so they stay float32 while the block stack runs in the requested `torch_dtype`;
657	        # align the activation with their parameter dtype.
658	        hidden_states = self.norm_out(hidden_states, temb, timestep_indices).to(get_parameter_dtype(self.proj_out))
659	        video_output = self.proj_out(hidden_states).index_select(1, video_indices)
660	        audio_output = self.audio_proj_out(hidden_states).index_select(1, audio_indices)
661	
662	        if not return_dict:
663	            return (video_output, audio_output)
664	        return MiniMaxH3TransformerOutput(sample=video_output, audio_sample=audio_output)
665
